title: Convergent validation: how Jason Cohen tells a real startup idea from polite "sounds good"
summary: Using Feynman's physics lectures as an analogy, Jason Cohen argues a real startup idea converges: the deeper you dig in customer interviews, the more people agree on the pain, the solution and the price. A false idea diverges into contradictory advice. He contrasts a divergent first idea with WP Engine, where 30 of 40 interviewees agreed to sign up.

principles.text: A real idea converges as you dig: more interviews bring more agreement on pain, solution and price.
principles.quote: my experience vetting WP Engine was convergent. The more people I spoke with, the more agreement there was over the pain they had, whether my solution was an acceptable, and the amount they were willing to spend.

principles.text: Everyone saying "great idea" means little; truth diverges when each person's details contradict the others.
principles.quote: Everyone said "That's a great idea, you should do it!" Except, as I dug in with each person, the "truth" started diverging.

principles.text: A true law holds up in novel situations; a shallow one crumbles outside its safe space. Test ideas the same way.
principles.quote: with Conservation of Energy, the closer we look the more powerful the law becomes, the more applications we have for it, the more accurate predictions it makes, and that is the characteristic of a bona fide Fundamental Law of the Universe.

principles.text: Strong validation is people agreeing to buy during the interview, at a clear price and feature set.
principles.quote: $50/mo to make a WordPress site fast, scalable, secure, and when tech support answers the phone, they should be knowledgeable about WordPress. Kick in a staging area and backups and it's a done deal. Thirty of forty people agreed to sign up during their interview.

principles.text: There is no rubric, but convergence or divergence feels strong if you are honest with yourself.
principles.quote: Of course there'll be no rubric to determine whether an idea is tenable or whether the situation is so bleak that you should give up. But in my experience this feeling of convergence or divergence is very strong

principles.text: Your hardest battle is biasing evidence toward validation; staying ignorant only makes the failure costlier.
principles.quote: Just remember how expensive it is to remain ignorant. You will meet the same, bitter end, only after a significantly larger investment in time, money, heart, and reputation.
